claim: Hdac3 is highly expressed in hematopoietic progenitors such as HSCs and CLP, and pDCs in spleen according to the ImmGen genome-wide expression dataset.
source: Genome-wide expression dataset ImmGen reveals that among class I HDACs, Hdac1, Hdac2, and Hdac3 but not Hdac8 are highly expressed by most immune cells. Hdac3 is highly expressed in hematopoietic progenitors such as HSCs and CLP, and pDCs in spleen (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to the ImmGen dataset and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing expression patterns.

claim: High expression of Hdac3 was observed in pDC progenitors, including HSCs, MMP4, CLP and CDPs, and bone marrow pDCs by RNA sequence analysis.
source: Consistently, high expression of Hdac3 was noticed in pDC progenitors, including HSCs, MMP4, CLP and CDPs, and bone marrow pDCs by RNA sequence analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: pDCs expressed significantly higher levels of Hdac3 than cDCs as analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR.
source: Furthermore, Hdac3 expression in sorted DC subsets analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) showed that pDCs expressed significantly higher levels of Hdac3 than cDCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: HDAC3 could be efficiently deleted in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice after tamoxifen treatment.
source: HDAC3 could be efficiently deleted in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D demonstrating deletion efficiency.

claim: Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice showed substantially reduced pDCs with absolute numbers decreased about fourfold in BM and spleens compared to Hdac3fl/fl mice.
source: Compared to Hdac3fl/fl mice, Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice showed substantially reduced pDCs and the absolute number decreased about fourfold in BM and spleens (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data and quantification shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: CD11chi cDCs were slightly decreased in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice, especially the CD24+CD172α− cDC1s, whereas the absolute numbers of CD24−CD172α+ cDC2s were comparable.
source: CD11chi cDCs were also slightly decreased, especially the CD24+CD172α− cDC1s, whereas the absolute numbers of CD24−CD172α+ cDC2s were comparable (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data and quantification shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The production of IFN-α by Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 bone marrow cells, splenocytes and splenic DCs was decreased in response to type A CpG ODN stimulation in vitro.
source: pDCs are the major producers of type-I IFN, consistent with the reduction of pDCs in BM and spleen of Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice, the production of IFN-α by Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 bone marrow cells, splenocytes and splenic DCs were also decreased in response to type A CpG ODN stimulation in vitro (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1D measuring IFN-α production.

claim: The percentage of splenic cDC1 marked by XCR1 showed little difference in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice compared with that of Hdac3fl/fl mice.
source: As shown in Figure 1E–G, in accordance with cDC1 identified by CD24, the percentage of splenic cDC1 marked by XCR1 showed little difference in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice compared with that of Hdac3fl/fl mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E–G.

claim: The expression of CD8α significantly decreased in HDAC3-deficient splenic cDC1 cells.
source: However, the expression of CD8α significantly decreased in HDAC3-deficient splenic cDC1 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing decreased CD8α expression.

claim: HDAC3 is required for pDC development in vivo.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated the requirement of HDAC3 in pDC development in vivo.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experimental results showing defective pDC development in HDAC3-deficient mice.

claim: The percentage of Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 BM-derived CD45.2+ cells were significantly lower than those derived from Hdac3fl/fl BM in competitive BM chimeric mice.
source: The percentage of Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 BM-derived CD45.2+ cells were significantly lower than those derived from Hdac3fl/fl BM, indicating a competitive disadvantage of the HDAC3-deficient BM cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from competitive BM chimera experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The percentage of CD45.2+ cells derived from Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 donors represented about 20% in BM and 30% in spleen of the chimeric mice.
source: The percentage of CD45.2+ cells derived from Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 donors only represented about 20% in BM and 30% in spleen of the chimeric mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The frequency of Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 derived BM and splenic pDCs among CD45.2+ cells decreased markedly in competitive BM chimeric mice.
source: Furthermore, the frequency of Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 derived BM and splenic pDCs among CD45.2+ cells also decreased markedly, whereas the frequency of splenic cDC subsets were not significantly disturbed (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A–C.

claim: Impaired pDC development from Hdac3 deleted BM cells was observed when BM cells were cultured in vitro for 5, 7, and 9 days in the presence of FLT3L and 4-hydroxytamoxifen.
source: Moreover, when the BM cells were cultured in vitro for 5, 7, and 9 days in the presence of FLT3L and 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) to induce Hdac3 deletion in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 BM cells, impaired pDC development from Hdac3 deleted BM cells was also observed, in line with the results from in vivo study (Figure 2D, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 2D, E.

claim: HDAC3 regulated pDC development in a cell intrinsic way.
source: These data suggested that HDAC3 regulated pDC development in a cell intrinsic way.
evidence: The claim is inferred from competitive BM chimera and in vitro culture experiments.

claim: The Lin−Sca-1+CD117+ (LSK) cells were increased significantly in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice compared to control mice.
source: Compared to control mice, the Lin−Sca-1+CD117+ (LSK) cells were increased significantly in Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of BM progenitor populations.

claim: CD150−CD48−Flt3− long-term HSC (LT-HSC) and CD150+ CD48−Flt3− short-term HSC (ST-HSC) were decreased in HDAC3-deficient mice.
source: Further analysis of LSK subpopulations (Klein et al., 2022; Pietras et al., 2015), we found that CD150−CD48−Flt3− long-term HSC (LT-HSC) and CD150+ CD48−Flt3− short-term HSC (ST-HSC) were decreased, CD150+CD48+Flt3− MPP2 and CD150−CD48+Flt3− MPP3 were dramatically increased, while the CD150−Flt3+ MMP4 was not significantly changed (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A–C and cites relevant literature (Klein et al., 2022; Pietras et al., 2015).

claim: CD150+CD48+Flt3− MPP2 and CD150−CD48+Flt3− MPP3 were dramatically increased in HDAC3-deficient mice.
source: Further analysis of LSK subpopulations (Klein et al., 2022; Pietras et al., 2015), we found that CD150−CD48−Flt3− long-term HSC (LT-HSC) and CD150+ CD48−Flt3− short-term HSC (ST-HSC) were decreased, CD150+CD48+Flt3− MPP2 and CD150−CD48+Flt3− MPP3 were dramatically increased, while the CD150−Flt3+ MMP4 was not significantly changed (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A–C and cites relevant literature (Klein et al., 2022; Pietras et al., 2015).

claim: HDAC3 deficiency led to markedly decreased number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32intCD34+ CMP.
source: Meanwhile, HDAC3 deficiency led to markedly decreased number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32intCD34+ CMP, while increased number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32+CD34+ granulocyte-macrophage progenitor (GMP), but comparable number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32−CD34− megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor (MEP) (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D–F.

claim: HDAC3 deficiency led to increased number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32+CD34+ granulocyte-macrophage progenitor (GMP).
source: Meanwhile, HDAC3 deficiency led to markedly decreased number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32intCD34+ CMP, while increased number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32+CD34+ granulocyte-macrophage progenitor (GMP), but comparable number of Sca-1−CD117+CD16/32−CD34− megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor (MEP) (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D–F.

claim: HDAC3-deficient mice showed a significant reduction in the numbers of CD115+CDP.
source: HDAC3-deficient mice showed a significant reduction in the numbers of CD115+CDP (Figure 3E–G) and CLP (Figure 3A–C), unexpectedly, the number of CD115−CDP cells were not significantly changed (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3E–G.

claim: HDAC3-deficient mice showed a significant reduction in the numbers of CLP.
source: HDAC3-deficient mice showed a significant reduction in the numbers of CD115+CDP (Figure 3E–G) and CLP (Figure 3A–C), unexpectedly, the number of CD115−CDP cells were not significantly changed (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A–C.

claim: The number of CD115−CDP cells were not significantly changed in HDAC3-deficient mice.
source: HDAC3-deficient mice showed a significant reduction in the numbers of CD115+CDP (Figure 3E–G) and CLP (Figure 3A–C), unexpectedly, the number of CD115−CDP cells were not significantly changed (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: HDAC3-deficient mice showed dramatically reduced pre-DC subsets.
source: When further analyzed the pre-DCs (Durai et al., 2019; Schlitzer et al., 2015), we found dramatically reduced pre-DC subsets, though the remaining pre-DCs were the cDC1-primed Siglec H−Ly6C− population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and cites relevant literature (Durai et al., 2019; Schlitzer et al., 2015).

claim: The remaining pre-DCs in HDAC3-deficient mice were the cDC1-primed Siglec H−Ly6C− population.
source: When further analyzed the pre-DCs (Durai et al., 2019; Schlitzer et al., 2015), we found dramatically reduced pre-DC subsets, though the remaining pre-DCs were the cDC1-primed Siglec H−Ly6C− population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and cites relevant literature (Durai et al., 2019; Schlitzer et al., 2015).

claim: HDAC3 was required for the passage of HSCs through regulating S phase and the formation of early lymphoid progenitors.
source: It was reported that HDAC3 was required for the passage of HSCs through regulating S phase and the formation of early lymphoid progenitors (Summers et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Summers et al., 2013.

claim: HDAC3-deficiency led to an increased percentage of BrdU-incorporated LSKs.
source: Compared with that of control cells, HDAC3-deficiency led to an increased percentage of BrdU-incorporated LSKs, but decreased proportion of BrdU-incorporated CLPs, and comparable ratios of BrdU-incorporated CD115−CDPs and CD115+CDPs, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU-incorporation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: HDAC3-deficiency led to decreased proportion of BrdU-incorporated CLPs.
source: Compared with that of control cells, HDAC3-deficiency led to an increased percentage of BrdU-incorporated LSKs, but decreased proportion of BrdU-incorporated CLPs, and comparable ratios of BrdU-incorporated CD115−CDPs and CD115+CDPs, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU-incorporation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The disturbed homeostasis of progenitor cells caused by HDAC3 deficiency might mainly due to their altered proliferation rates.
source: These results suggested that the disturbed homeostasis of progenitor cells caused by HDAC3 deficiency might mainly due to their altered proliferation rates.
evidence: The claim is inferred from BrdU-incorporation assay results showing altered proliferation in different progenitor populations.

claim: HDAC3-deficient LSKs and CD115−CDPs showed significant competitive disadvantage in BM chimeric mice.
source: HDAC3-deficient LSKs and CD115−CDPs showed significant competitive disadvantage, revealed by the very low percentage of CD45.2+ cells in chimeric mice generated with HDAC3-deficient progenitors compared with that of Hdac3fl/fl progenitors (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by BM chimera transplantation data shown in Figure 4B–C.

claim: A decreased frequency of pDCs derived from HDAC3-deficient CD115−CDP was detected in both BM and spleen of chimeric mice.
source: Furthermore, a decreased frequency of pDCs derived from HDAC3-deficient CD115−CDP was detected in both BM and spleen, whereas the frequencies of cDC subsets in the spleen were comparable to that derived from control CD115−CDP.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of BM chimeric mice.

claim: HDAC3 deficiency in CD115−CDPs resulted in severe defect in pDC, but not in cDC development.
source: These results indicated that HDAC3 deficiency in CD115−CDPs resulted in severe defect in pDC, but not in cDC development (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: HDAC3 deficiency resulted in down-regulation of 2533 and up-regulation of 206 genes with annotations in LMPPs.
source: HDAC3 deficiency resulted in down-regulation of 2533 and up-regulation of 206 genes with annotations in LMPPs (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: KEGG pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes in HDAC3-deficient LMPPs revealed a significant enrichment of genes for hematopoietic lineage pathway.
source: KEGG pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes revealed a significant enrichment of genes for hematopoietic lineage pathway (Figure 4G), suggesting that HDAC3 may play important roles in hematopoietic linage cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: HDAC3-deficient CD115−CDPs showed down regulated expression of genes that are highly expressed in pDC, such as Siglech, Ly6c2, Ly6d, Cd209a, and Cox6a2.
source: Interestingly, the HDAC3-deficient CD115−CDPs showed down regulated expression of genes that are highly expressed in pDC, such as Siglech, Ly6c2, Ly6d, Cd209a, and Cox6a2 (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Myeloid-related genes such as Mpo, Ctsg, and Ms4a3 were up-regulated in both LMPP and CD115−CDPs upon HDAC3 deficiency.
source: In addition, myeloid-related genes such as Mpo, Ctsg, and Ms4a3 were up-regulated, but pDC-associated genes such as Siglech, Ly6d, and Ly6c2 were down-regulated in both LMPP and CD115−CDPs (Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: pDC-associated genes such as Siglech, Ly6d, and Ly6c2 were down-regulated in both LMPP and CD115−CDPs upon HDAC3 deficiency.
source: In addition, myeloid-related genes such as Mpo, Ctsg, and Ms4a3 were up-regulated, but pDC-associated genes such as Siglech, Ly6d, and Ly6c2 were down-regulated in both LMPP and CD115−CDPs (Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: HDAC3 is crucial for the expression of pDC-associated genes in progenitors.
source: These results indicated that HDAC3 is crucial for the expression of pDC-associated genes in those progenitors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from RNA-seq data showing altered gene expression in HDAC3-deficient progenitors.

claim: HDAC3-deficient LSKs and CD115−CDPs were defective to differentiate into pDCs even though with increased cell numbers.
source: Overall, these results indicated that HDAC3-deficient LSKs and CD115−CDPs were defective to differentiate into pDCs even though with increased cell numbers.
evidence: The claim is inferred from transplantation experiments and RNA-seq data.

claim: Both pDCs and cDCs generated from HDAC3-deficient LMPPs decreased significantly in vitro.
source: Both pDCs and cDCs generated from HDAC3-deficient LMPPs decreased significantly.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro culture data.

claim: HDAC3-deficient Flt3+CMPs, CLPs, CD115+CDPs and CD115-CDPs all showed profound defective pDC development in vitro, with no or slight reduction in cDC development.
source: Whereas HDAC3-deficient Flt3+CMPs, CLPs, CD115+CDPs and CD115-CDPs all showed profound defective pDC development in vitro, with no or slight reduction in cDC development (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figure 5A–B.

claim: pDCs and cDCs could develop normally in the spleen of Hdac3fl/fl Itgax-Cre mice.
source: As shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D, pDCs and cDCs could develop normally in the spleen of Hdac3fl/fl Itgax-Cre mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: HDAC3 was required for pDC development from all early progenitors with DC differentiation potential, but dispensable for the later pDC differentiation.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated that HDAC3 was required for pDC development from all early progenitors with DC differentiation potential, but dispensable for the later pDC differentiation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from in vitro culture experiments with different progenitors and Itgax-Cre deletion experiments.

claim: HDAC3 has been reported to be a dichotomous transcriptional activator and repressor during the activation of macrophages by LPS, with a non-canonical deacetylase-independent function to activate gene expression.
source: HDAC3 has been reported to be a dichotomous transcriptional activator and repressor during the activation of macrophages by LPS, with a non-canonical deacetylase-independent function to activate gene expression (Nguyen et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Nguyen et al., 2020.

claim: At low concentration, RGFP966 could efficiently inhibit the differentiation of pDCs but not for cDCs.
source: At low concentration, RGFP966 could efficiently inhibit the differentiation of pDCs but not for cDCs.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro culture experiments with RGFP966.

claim: HDAC3 deacetylase activity was required preferentially for pDC development.
source: This result suggested that HDAC3 deacetylase activity was required preferentially for pDC development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from RGFP966 inhibitor experiments.

claim: HDAC3 (Y298F) mutant contains a tyrosine-to-phenylalanine substitution at residue 298, which inactivates HDAC3 deacetylase catalytic activity but not the interaction with NCoR/SMRT.
source: HDAC3 (Y298F) mutant contains a tyrosine-to-phenylalanine substitution at residue 298, which inactivates HDAC3 deacetylase catalytic activity but not the interaction with NCoR/SMRT (Sun et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sun et al., 2013.

claim: The development of pDC from HDAC3-deficient Lin− BM cells could be partially rescued by transducing the wild-type HDAC3.
source: The development of pDC from HDAC3-deficient Lin− BM cells could be partially rescued by transducing the wild-type HDAC3.
evidence: The claim is supported by retroviral transduction rescue experiments.

claim: Transduction of the deacetylase-inactivated HDAC3 (Y298F) mutant did not restore pDC development from HDAC3-deficient Lin− BM cells.
source: However, transduction of the deacetylase-inactivated HDAC3 (Y298F) mutant did not restore pDC development from HDAC3-deficient Lin− BM cells (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by retroviral transduction rescue experiments shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: The deacetylase activity of HDAC3 is essential for its role in regulating the development of pDCs.
source: Together, these results indicated that the deacetylase activity of HDAC3 is essential for its role in regulating the development of pDCs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from RGFP966 inhibitor experiments and Y298F mutant rescue experiments.

claim: HDAC3-deficient pDCs showed down-regulated pDC signature genes such as transcription factor Tcf4 and pDC surface molecules Siglech, Ly6c1, Ly6c2, and Ly6d.
source: Consistent with RNA-seq results obtained from progenitors, HDAC3-deficient pDCs showed enhanced enrichment of cell-cycle and cell proliferation process (Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1), however, down-regulated pDC signature genes such as transcription factor Tcf4 and pDC surface molecules Siglech, Ly6c1, Ly6c2, and Ly6d (Figure 7A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7A–D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Among up-regulated genes in HDAC3-deficient pDCs, some genes were required in cDC1 development, such as Spi1, Zfp366, Batf3 and Id2.
source: Among up-regulated genes in HDAC3-deficient pDCs, some genes were required in cDC1 development, such as Spi1 (Dakic et al., 2005; Carotta et al., 2010; Chopin et al., 2019), Zfp366 (Zhang et al., 2021), Batf3 (Hildner et al., 2008; Grajales-Reyes et al., 2015) and Id2 (Jackson et al., 2011; Schlitzer et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data and multiple citations (Dakic et al., 2005; Carotta et al., 2010; Chopin et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2021; Hildner et al., 2008; Grajales-Reyes et al., 2015; Jackson et al., 2011; Schlitzer et al., 2015).

claim: Specific marker of cDC specification Zbtb46 and the surface molecule highly expressed by cDC1, such as Clec9a were up-regulated in HDAC3-deficient pDCs.
source: Specific marker of cDC specification Zbtb46 (Meredith et al., 2012a; Meredith et al., 2012b) and the surface molecule highly expressed by cDC1, such as Clec9a were also up-regulated in HDAC3-deficient pDCs.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citations (Meredith et al., 2012a; Meredith et al., 2012b).

claim: HDAC3-deficient pDCs displayed a cDC-biased transcriptional profile.
source: These results displayed a cDC-biased transcriptional profile in HDAC3-deficient pDCs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from RNA-seq data showing upregulation of cDC-associated genes and downregulation of pDC-associated genes.

claim: HDAC3 associates with NCoR/SMRT to form co-repressor complex and represses gene expression by suppressing histone acetylation modifications.
source: HDAC3 associates with NCoR/SMRT to form co-repressor complex and represses gene expression by suppressing histone acetylation modifications.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about HDAC3 function.

claim: Motif analysis of unique H3K27ac peaks in HDAC3-deficient pDCs showed that these regions were significantly enriched with motifs recognized by PU.1 (SPI1).
source: Motif analysis of unique H3K27ac peaks in HDAC3-deficient pDCs showed that these regions were significantly enriched with motifs recognized by PU.1 (SPI1) (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT&Tag motif analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: PU.1 promotes cDC development while repress pDC development by activating Zfp366 expression.
source: PU.1 promotes cDC development while repress pDC development by activating Zfp366 expression (Chopin et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chopin et al., 2019.

claim: HDAC3-deficient pDCs showed enhanced H3K27ac level around PU.1-binding region at cDC1-associated gene loci, including transcription factor Zfp366, Zbtb46, Batf3 and cDC surface molecule CD80, CD83 gene loci.
source: HDAC3-deficient pDCs showed enhanced H3K27ac level around PU.1-binding region at cDC1-associated gene loci, including transcription factor Zfp366, Zbtb46, Batf3 and cDC surface molecule CD80, CD83 gene loci (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT&Tag data shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Significantly higher enrichments of HDAC3 on the sites of Zfp366, Zbtb46, Batf3 loci than that of IgG control were observed in BM pDCs.
source: As shown in Figure 7F, significantly higher enrichments of HDAC3 on the sites of Zfp366, Zbtb46, Batf3 loci than that of IgG control were observed.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: pDC development from Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 BM cells were severely defective in BM chimeric mice analyzed 3 weeks after tamoxifen treatment.
source: Analysis of CD45.2+ donor cells showed that pDC development from Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 BM cells were severely defective.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of long-term BM chimeric mice.

claim: The percentage and absolute number of splenic cDC1 derived from Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 BM cells were increased in long-term BM chimeric mice.
source: Meanwhile, the percentage and absolute number of splenic cDC1 derived from Hdac3fl/fl CreERT2 BM cells were increased, while that of cDC2 were decreased (Figure 7G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7G and H.

claim: HDAC3 could repress cDC1-associated gene expression through histone deacetylation and thereby promoted the expression of pDC-associated genes and subsequent pDC development.
source: Taken together, these results suggested that HDAC3 could repress cDC1-associated gene expression through histone deacetylation and thereby promoted the expression of pDC-associated genes and subsequent pDC development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from CUT&Tag, ChIP-qPCR, RNA-seq, and BM chimera experiments.

claim: HDAC3 is a key epigenetic regulator for pDC development.
source: In this study, we identified HDAC3 as a key epigenetic regulator for pDC development, evidenced by the absence of pDCs in BM and spleens of the HDAC3-deficient mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental results showing defective pDC development in HDAC3-deficient mice.

claim: HDAC3 deficiency resulted in disturbed homeostasis of BM hematopoietic progenitors with DC differentiation potential.
source: Further investigation revealed that HDAC3 deficiency resulted in disturbed homeostasis of BM hematopoietic progenitors with DC differentiation potential.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of progenitor populations.

claim: HDAC3 regulated the acetylation of H3K27 at cDC1-associated gene loci, thereby repressed the expression of cDC1-associated genes and promoted the expression of pDC-associated genes and subsequent differentiation of the progenitors towards pDCs.
source: The results suggested that HDAC3 regulated the acetylation of H3K27 at cDC1-associated gene loci, thereby repressed the expression of cDC1-associated genes and promoted the expression of pDC-associated genes and subsequent differentiation of the progenitors towards pDCs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from CUT&Tag, ChIP-qPCR, and RNA-seq data.

claim: The study revealed a novel epigenetic regulatory role of HDAC3 in pDC development.
source: Thus, our study revealed a novel epigenetic regulatory role of HDAC3 in pDC development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Deletion of Hdac3 resulted in marked decrease in the numbers of CMPs, CLPs and CD115+CDPs.
source: We observed that deletion of Hdac3 resulted in marked decrease in the numbers of CMPs, CLPs and CD115+CDPs, which partially accounted for the reduced pDC generation, whereas the numbers of HDAC3-deficient LSKs, especially MPP2 and MPP3, were significantly increased.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of progenitor populations.

claim: The numbers of HDAC3-deficient LSKs, especially MPP2 and MPP3, were significantly increased.
source: We observed that deletion of Hdac3 resulted in marked decrease in the numbers of CMPs, CLPs and CD115+CDPs, which partially accounted for the reduced pDC generation, whereas the numbers of HDAC3-deficient LSKs, especially MPP2 and MPP3, were significantly increased.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of progenitor populations.

claim: Despite the increase in the numbers of LSKs, their abilities to differentiate into pDCs were severely impaired.
source: However, despite the increase in the numbers, their abilities to differentiate into pDCs were severely impaired.
evidence: The claim is supported by transplantation experiments showing defective pDC differentiation from HDAC3-deficient LSKs.

claim: The reduction in the number of CLP and increase in the number of LSKs in HDAC3-deficient mice were in line with the results of the BrdU incorporation analysis.
source: The reduction in the number of CLP and increase in the number of LSKs in HDAC3-deficient mice were in line with the results of the BrdU incorporation analysis that showed a reduced DNA replication in HDAC3-deficient CLPs and an increased DNA synthesis in HDAC3-deficient LSKs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing progenitor numbers with BrdU incorporation data.

claim: A decrease of Csf1r (coding CD115) expression could be observed in RNA-seq analysis of the HDAC3-deficient CDPs.
source: Considering that total number of CDPs did not change significantly, and a decrease of Csf1r (coding CD115) expression could be observed in RNA-seq analysis of the HDAC3-deficient CDPs.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data of HDAC3-deficient CDPs.

claim: The reserved number of CD115-CDPs might be due to the downregulation of Csf1r expression in CD115+CDPs.
source: These results suggested that the reserved number of CD115-CDPs might be due to the downregulation of Csf1r expression in CD115+CDPs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from RNA-seq data showing decreased Csf1r expression and flow cytometry data showing unchanged CD115-CDP numbers.

claim: HDAC3 regulated different hematopoietic progenitors with different regulator mechanisms.
source: Overall, these results suggested that HDAC3 regulated different hematopoietic progenitors with different regulator mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is inferred from differential effects of HDAC3 deficiency on different progenitor populations.

claim: PU.1-DC-SCRIPT-IRF8 axis is an important transcriptional pathway that regulated the fate determination between pDC and cDC1.
source: Recent studies reported PU.1-DC-SCRIPT-IRF8 axis as an important transcriptional pathway that regulated the fate determination between pDC and cDC1.
evidence: The claim is based on recent studies cited in the discussion.

claim: PU.1 can activate Zfp366 (encodes DC-SCRIPT) expression and DC-SCRIPT enhanced the expression of Irf8 and thereby promoted the development and function of cDC1.
